REPORT
Date October 17, 1938.

Subject Books entitled "The First Year" and "Breaking Through the
Cordon Around Hsuchow."

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. MacAdie.

At 10.15 a.m., October 17, Special Branch detectives
visited the Yuan Tung (遠東) Bookstore, 378 Foochow Road
and seized 91 copies of the book "The First Year," a
publication containing anti-Japanese propaganda. Copies of
a similar publication entitled "Breaking through the Cordon
Around Hsuchow" had been sold out.

While the acting manager of the bookstore named Wong
Siao-bing (黃曉蘋) assured detectives that no copies of
"The First Year" other than those visible on the show counters
were in stock, another fifty copies were found upstairs.

Questioned regarding the source of this book, the manager
stated that it had been supplied by one Chen (陳) a student
of the Hwa Hwa Middle School, Lane 584, No4, Foochow Road.

With regard to the book "Breaking Through the Cordon
Around Hsuchow," the manager stated that this book was mailed
from an address in Hongkong, No.15 Wong Tu Da Dao (王后大道)
(Queen's Street?) Hongkong.

The manager was instructed to call at Special Branch
together with the student named Chen on the afternoon of
October 17, in order to receive the decision of D.C. (Special
Branch).

D. S. I.

Translation of a poem appearing in a book entitled
"The First Year" (第一年) published on September 30, 1938:-

ON THE POST

Let us hold our weapons firmly
Whilst on our post
And show our indignation
Without hesitation!
Let us use our pens
To analyze the shameless deeds
Committed by the enemy,
And expose the secrets
In the hearts of the enemy!
Let us make use of our education
To attack the desperadoes
Who are invading our territory!
With song and gun at the front,
Let us fire, fire continuously
At the followers of XX Fascists!
We should not hesitate!
We should not be afraid,
For we have weapons
Bequeathed to us thousands of years ago!
We must make known to the whole world
The shameless acts of the enemy;
Her use of poison gas for the massacre of Chinese people;
Her indiscriminate and aimless bombing from the air
That has killed hundreds of thousands of Chinese.
We will make known to the entire world
The looting, the beastly acts, the rape
Committed by the enemy;
People killed in cool blood with bayonets;
Batch after batch of Chinese mercilessly slaughtered;
The piratical activities along the coast;

- 2 -

The unlawful removal to Tokyo from Tientsin and Peiping
Of our state treasures;
The hoisting of Chinese flags by enemy warships
In the Whangpoo River;
All these constitute the Bushido spirit of the emey!
Our songs we regard as our weapons
And the only aim of our nation
Is to overthrow XX Imperialism.

(Reproduced from the National Salvation
Daily News)

Translation of extracts from book entitled "Breaking
Through the Cordon Around Hsuchow" (徐州突圍)
published in September 1938

Page 1
Under merciless bombing by enemy planes,
hospitals and houses in Hsuchow were reduced to ashes;
even the Catholic Church, which had a cross on top and
which was flying a French flag, was wrecked by the
Imperial Army. The disregard of world justice and
righteousness by the Japanese Fascist robbers can be
proved by irreputable evidence. All Powers should
realize that the invasion of China by the Japanese Fascist
robbers is not a simple problem affecting the Orient
alone; it is a problem of world importance.

Page 68
The cruel, beastly Japanese warlords! We
will take vengeance and settle this bloody account!

Pages 81/2
At every village, the robber troops stripped
the women of their clothing. Many women who would not
stand such humiliation were killed by the soldiers.
Seven robber soldiers went to Chow Za Village in North
Kiangsu and raped the women there. Two of the soldiers
were killed by the people. Other robber troops later
arrived and massacred more than 270 villagers including
women and children.

Page 165
Can the Japanese aeroplanes bomb every
Chinese village to ruins? Can the Japanese cover all
the territory of China? One day the Japanese tanks

-2-

will turn around madly like headless flies until they are
tired out and are carried away by tenacious ants. Chinese
farmers will ride on horses of the Japanese cavalry and wave
the flag of mobile units behind the Japanese lines, and the
"long flourishing" Imperial Army will find it difficult to
remain peacefully in any Chinese village. While the
Chinese regular troops withdraw outside the cordon drawn
up around them, the Chinese people will remain within the
circle to dig a sufficient number of graves for you!

The "Employee" (取負), a ten-day periodical (printed
by the Wenchow Wen Min Printing Company (温州文明印刷局),
published the following articles in its first issue on
April 1, 1938 :-

THE FIRST ISSUE OF THE PERIODICAL

Shanghai fell into the hands of the enemy after
the withdrawal of the Chinese forces from Nantao and local
conditions underwent a great change. Periodicals that were
worthy of reading in the past and utilized in the work for
the salvation of the nation suspended publication..
Shanghai, a centre of civilization, is now an "isolated island".

The devils have destroyed all our cultural
enterprises in this "isolated island". Many workers have
suffered greatly. Yet we should not lose our spirit because
of this unfavourable circumstances; we should continue our
determined struggle with the enemy.

We hope that employees living in this "isolated
island" will discuss world affairs during their leisure hours.
We must all take part in the work of national salvation and
conduct a stubborn struggle with our enemy and its running
dogs.

----------

CHINESE MOBILE UNITS RECAPTURE TSINGPU : ENEMY PACIFICATION
SECTION ENTIRELY WIPED OUT

There are 2,000 members of the Chinese mobile units
stationed along Loh Hwa Li (六華里) and Sung Keng (沈巷),
south of Tsu Ka Kuoh (朱家角), Tsingpu Hsien. They are
under the leadership of Wu Pah-tseu (吳伯州).

Upon learning that the Japanese soldiers inside
the city of Tsingpu had been transferred and that only a
small number of armed members of the Pacification Section

- 2 -

were stationed there, the leader on March 16 detailed 40 men
in plain clothes to enter the city. The men surrounded
the Japanese Pacification Section whose office is located
in the Maintenance Association and ordered them to lay down
their arms. A clash took place, in the course of which
most of the members of the Pacification Section were killed.
The Japanese flag hoisted at the Maintenance Association was
torn to pieces and was replaced by a Kuomintang flag.
The city of Tsingpu was thus retaken by the Chinese.

On the following day, 500 Japanese soldiers were
sent to Tsu Ka Kuch. In the meantime, another 500 Japanese
soldiers had arrived at Tien Mo San (天目山) as a reserve.
On the morning of March 18, the Japanese attacked Sung Kong
from two directions. Serious fighting ensued, lasting half
a day. Some 170 Japanese soldiers were either killed or
wounded, while Chinese mobile units lost 100 men. Another
serious engagement took place in the neighbourhood on the
morning of March 19, resulting in many casualties to both sides.

The Japanese soldiers were angry at the farmers
in the vicinity of Sung Kong. They killed all the able-bodied
farmers and raped the women. More than ten women lost their
lives when they resisted. Six of the women who had been
raped committed suicide. A girl of only 12 years of age
was also mercilessly molested. Some 20 girls whose ages
ranged from one to six were killed.

After committing these atrocious acts, the
Japanese set fire to the villages. The farmers sustained
heavy losses.
